summary: Layer SF.4 of the scheme-foundations roadmap, planned at target level in 57 nodes. (a) Infinitesimal lifting: first-order thickenings, formally smooth/unramified/étale morphisms of schemes, the infinitesimal lifting criterion and the torsor of infinitesimal lifts, extending Mathlib's ring-level formal smoothness and scheme-level formal unramifiedness. (b) Deformation theory: the Artinian coefficient category C_Λ, deformation functors with Schlessinger's conditions, hulls, Schlessinger's theorem, obstruction theories, square-zero deformations classified by the naive cotangent complex (the full cotangent complex is not used), deformations of smooth schemes and line bundles, and the versal deformation of a node. (c) Formal geometry: Spf of adic rings with finitely generated ideal of definition, formal schemes, formal completion, coherent formal modules. (d) Algebraization: theorem on formal functions, Stein factorization, Grothendieck's existence and algebraization theorems with comparison to the completion, and effectivity of formal deformations of curves. (e) Modifications kept distinct from alterations: modifications, strict transforms, generic flatness, Raynaud–Gruson flattening by blowup, domination of modifications by admissible blowups, Chow's lemma; resolution only in the named setting of curves (normalization). (f) The moduli input to alterations, moved down from higher-tier owners: Grassmannians, Hilbert and Quot schemes, the stack of stable pointed curves, finiteness of Isom, algebraicity, properness and smoothness, the level-structure finite cover, and extension of stable pointed curves after an alteration. (g) de Jong's alterations: alterations, regular schemes, strict normal crossings divisors, split semistable curves, local structure and resolution of nodal families over regular bases, curve fibrations, the stable-model domination lemma, Theorem 5.8, Theorem 4.1 and, over traits, strict semistable pairs and Theorem 6.5. Models over a DVR with base, generic fibre and base extension, semistable and stable reduction of curves, and blowups are imported from Tau Ceti StableReduction (Layers 0–4, 7–9); Néron models and abelian semistable reduction are owned by NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties, which builds on SF.4 rather than feeding it. Independent review corrects source hypotheses and prototype signatures; coverage is partial and the review is needs_changes pending the explicitly recorded bridges and reader synchronization.

nodes.title: First-order thickenings of schemes
nodes.statement: A thickening of schemes is a closed immersion i : T → T′ whose underlying map of spaces is a bijection (equivalently, on every affine chart its defining ideal consists of nilpotent elements; a uniform nilpotence exponent on an open neighbourhood additionally follows when that ideal is finitely generated). It is a first-order thickening when I² = 0 and a finite-order thickening when Iⁿ = 0 for some n. For a first-order thickening the conormal sheaf C_{T/T′} = I/I² is I itself, a quasi-coherent O_T-module. A thickening over a base S is a thickening in the category of S-schemes. In Mathlib vocabulary the predicate on i is: IsClosedImmersion i together with i.ker * i.ker = ⊥ (first order) or IsNilpotent i.ker (finite order), using the ideal sheaf i.ker of Mathlib's IdealSheafData.
hypotheses: Schemes and morphisms are those of Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme; no Noetherian hypothesis.
Affine first-order thickenings Spec(B/J) → Spec B with J² = 0 are the test objects of the lifting definitions.
proofSteps: Define the predicate by the closed-immersion condition and the vanishing of the square of the kernel ideal sheaf (Stacks 04EX, Definition 37.2.1).
On an affine chart Spec B the ideal sheaf of Spec(B/J) is the quasi-coherent ideal J~, so the affine characterisation is J² = 0.

Base change of a first-order thickening along any T′-scheme is again a first-order thickening, because the base-changed ideal is the image of I ⊗ O and its square is the image of I² (Stacks Section 37.2).

A finite-order thickening factors as a finite chain of first-order thickenings T = T_1 ⊂ T_2 ⊂ … ⊂ T_n = T′ cut out by the powers I^k, which reduces lifting along nilpotent ideals to the square-zero case (the reduction used in Mathlib's Algebra.FormallySmooth.exists_lift).
acceptance: Spec k → Spec k[ε] is a first-order thickening and Spec k → Spec k[x]/(x³) is a thickening that is not first order.
Agreement with the hypothesis shape of Mathlib's FormallyUnramified.hom_ext (closed immersion with nilpotent kernel).

nodes.title: Formally smooth, formally unramified and formally étale morphisms of schemes
nodes.statement: A morphism f : X → S of schemes is formally smooth (respectively formally unramified, formally étale) if for every first-order thickening T ⊂ T′ of affine schemes over S, every S-morphism T → X extends to at least one (respectively at most one, exactly one) S-morphism T′ → X. Formally étale is equivalent to formally smooth and formally unramified. For X = Spec B and S = Spec A formal smoothness of f is formal smoothness of the ring map A → B; Mathlib defines the latter (Algebra.FormallySmooth) by Ω_{B/A} projective and H¹(L_{B/A}) = 0 and proves the equivalence with square-zero lifting. Formal unramifiedness of schemes agrees with Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry.FormallyUnramified.
hypotheses: No finiteness hypothesis on f.
The test thickenings T ⊂ T′ are affine; Zariski-locality (Stacks 0D0F) shows the lifting property then holds for every first-order thickening when the obstruction group vanishes.
proofSteps: Define the three predicates by the lifting properties against affine first-order thickenings over S (Stacks 02H0, 02H8, 02HG).
Prove formally étale ⟺ formally smooth and formally unramified (Stacks 02HH, Lemma 37.11.4), mirroring Mathlib's Algebra.FormallyEtale.iff_formallyUnramified_and_formallySmooth.

Prove the affine comparison: for affine X and S the predicate is Algebra.FormallySmooth of the ring map (Stacks 02H4, Lemma 37.11.6), using Mathlib's Algebra.FormallySmooth.exists_lift and the converse test Algebra.FormallySmooth.iff_split_surjection.

Prove Zariski-locality on source and target (Stacks 0D0F, Lemma 37.11.10): the sheaf of local lifts is a torsor under the quasi-coherent Hom sheaf of pulled-back differentials into the square-zero ideal. The affine H¹-vanishing argument in Stacks 0D0E, Lemma 37.11.9, glues those lifts without using the later smooth-scheme deformation classification.
Stability under composition and base change follows from the lifting definition.
acceptance: Affine space 𝔸(n; S) → S is formally smooth (Mathlib's Algebra.instFormallySmoothMvPolynomial).
A closed immersion Spec(A/I) → Spec A with I ≠ I² is formally unramified but not formally smooth.

nodes.title: Infinitesimal lifting criterion
nodes.statement: Let f : X → S be locally of finite presentation. Then f is smooth (Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth) iff f is formally smooth; f is étale iff f is formally étale; and f is unramified in the finitely presented sense iff f is formally unramified. In particular a smooth morphism admits extensions along every first-order thickening of affine schemes over S, and an étale morphism admits unique extensions.
hypotheses: f locally of finite presentation (needed for the forward implications from formal to actual smoothness and étaleness).
proofSteps: Reduce to affine X and S using Zariski-locality of both sides: Mathlib's Smooth is affine-local with ring property RingHom.Smooth, and formal smoothness is Zariski-local by SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/formally-smooth-morphism (Stacks 0D0F).

On affines, Mathlib's Algebra.Smooth is by definition formally smooth plus finitely presented (Stacks 00TN, Algebra Proposition 10.138.13), which with the affine comparison of formal smoothness gives the smooth case (Stacks 02H6, Lemma 37.11.7).

The converse direction for a non-affine source uses that the sheaf of local lifts is a torsor under Hom(a*Ω_{X/S}, I) (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/smooth-lifting-torsor) and that its class in H¹ of a quasi-coherent sheaf on an affine scheme vanishes (Stacks 0D0E).
Étale and unramified cases: Stacks 02HM (Lemma 37.8.10) and 02HE (Lemma 37.6.9), with Mathlib's Etale.iff_flat_and_formallyUnramified for the comparison with Mathlib's étale class.
acceptance: Affine space and open immersions satisfy the lifting property. Spec k[x]/(x²) → Spec k is not formally smooth: the map x ↦ y from Spec k[y]/(y²) does not extend over the first-order thickening Spec k[y]/(y²) ⊂ Spec k[y]/(y³), since every extension sends x to an element y + cy² whose square y² is nonzero.

sources.match: States that a morphism is smooth exactly when it is locally of finite presentation and formally smooth, with the étale and unramified analogues, proved by reduction to the algebra statement.

nodes.title: Torsor of infinitesimal lifts
nodes.statement: Let S be a scheme, T ⊂ T′ a first-order thickening over S with ideal I (an O_T-module), X → S a morphism and a : T → X an S-morphism. (1) The presheaf on T′ sending an open U′ to the set of S-morphisms U′ → X extending a on U′ ∩ T is a sheaf, and Hom_{O_T}(a*Ω_{X/S}, I) acts on it simply transitively wherever sections exist (a pseudo-torsor). (2) If X → S is formally smooth, local extensions exist, so this is a torsor; its class in H¹(T, Hom(a*Ω_{X/S}, I)) is the obstruction to a global extension. (3) If T is affine and Ω_{X/S} is locally projective (for instance X → S smooth) the class vanishes and an extension exists. (4) If X → S is formally étale the extension exists and is unique.
hypotheses: Ω_{X/S} is the quasi-coherent sheaf of relative Kähler differentials; local projectivity of Ω_{X/S} holds for formally smooth f (Stacks 06B5).
proofSteps: Two extensions agreeing on T differ by an O_S-derivation O_X → a_*I, equivalently an O_T-linear map a*Ω_{X/S} → I (Stacks 04FG, Lemma 37.9.1); conversely a derivation modifies an extension (Stacks 02H5, Lemma 37.9.2). On affine charts this is Mathlib's derivationToSquareZeroEquivLift combined with KaehlerDifferential.linearMapEquivDerivation.
The presheaf of local extensions is a sheaf (Stacks 04FH, Lemma 37.9.4) and the action is simply transitive where nonempty (Stacks 04FJ, Lemma 37.9.5; Remark 04FK).
Torsors under an abelian sheaf are classified by H¹ (Stacks 02FQ, Lemma 20.4.3); with the scheme-module cohomology of Tau Ceti (Scheme.Modules.Cohomology) this gives the obstruction class.
If T is affine and the Hom sheaf has vanishing H¹ (Stacks 0D0E, Lemma 37.11.9) the torsor is trivial.
acceptance: For X = 𝔸¹_S and a section over T, the set of extensions to T′ is a torsor under Γ(T, I); for X étale over S it is a single point.

sources.match: Describes the difference of two infinitesimal extensions as a derivation, the sheaf of local extensions with its simply transitive action by Hom(a*Ω, C), the classification of torsors by H¹ and the vanishing of H¹ on affines for locally projective Ω.
The global-lift obstruction in H¹ is the argument inside this proof rather than a separately numbered lemma.

nodes.title: Artinian coefficient categories and small extensions
nodes.statement: Fix a Noetherian ring Λ and a finite ring map Λ → k to a field (the classical case: Λ a complete Noetherian local ring with residue field k). The category C_Λ has as objects Artinian local Λ-algebras A together with a Λ-algebra identification A/m_A ≅ k, and as morphisms local Λ-algebra homomorphisms compatible with the identifications. The category Ĉ_Λ is defined in the same way with complete Noetherian local Λ-algebras with residue field k. A small extension is a surjection A′ → A in C_Λ whose kernel is a nonzero principal ideal annihilated by m_{A′}. The dual numbers k[ε] are the object k ⊕ kε with ε² = 0.
hypotheses: Λ Noetherian; Λ → k finite (in the classical case, Λ complete local with residue field k).
Objects carry a fixed residue identification; morphisms respect it.
For the classical hull and power-series criteria, Λ is a complete Noetherian local ring and Λ → k is its residue-field quotient (surjective with kernel m_Λ).
proofSteps: Define the full subcategory of Λ-algebras with the stated properties; Artinian local means Noetherian with nilpotent maximal ideal (Mathlib isArtinianRing_iff_isNilpotent_maximalIdeal) (Stacks 06GC, Definition 90.3.1).
Every surjection in C_Λ factors as a finite composite of small extensions, by filtering the kernel by m-stable ideals of length one (Stacks 06GE, Lemma 90.3.3).
Fibre products A₁ ×_A A₂ lie in C_Λ when one of the two maps is surjective, and the base change of a small extension is a small extension (Stacks 06GH, Lemma 90.3.8).
An object of Ĉ_Λ is the inverse limit of its Artinian quotients R/m^n, which lie in C_Λ (Stacks 06GW, Definition 90.4.1; Mathlib's AdicCompletion and IsAdicComplete for the comparison).
acceptance: Z/p^n ∈ C_{Z_p} with k = F_p; Z_p ∈ Ĉ_{Z_p} but not in C_{Z_p}.
k[ε] ×_k k[ε] ≅ k[ε₁, ε₂]/(ε₁, ε₂)².

nodes.title: Deformation functors and Schlessinger's conditions
nodes.statement: A predeformation functor is a functor F : C_Λ → Set with F(k) a single point. For morphisms A′ → A and A″ → A in C_Λ consider the natural map θ : F(A′ ×_A A″) → F(A′) ×_{F(A)} F(A″). Schlessinger's conditions are: (H1) θ is surjective whenever A″ → A is a small extension; (H2) θ is bijective when A = k and A″ = k[ε]; (H3) the tangent space T_F = F(k[ε]) is finite-dimensional; (H4) θ is bijective whenever A′ = A″ → A is a small extension. Under (H2), T_F carries a natural k-vector space structure. A deformation functor is a predeformation functor satisfying the Rim–Schlessinger condition, which for functors is (H4) together with (H1) and (H2) for all such pairs. For a category cofibred in groupoids satisfying (RS), the functor of isomorphism classes satisfies (H1) and (H2), but need not satisfy (H4): automorphisms can obstruct injectivity of the comparison map (Stacks 06JA).
hypotheses: F(k) a singleton.
Conditions are stated for all objects of C_Λ; (H3) uses the vector-space structure given by (H2).
proofSteps: Package the conditions as predicates on functors C_Λ → Set (Stacks 06HW, Definition 90.10.1, with Remark 06HY identifying (S1), (S2) with (H1), (H2) for functors; 0D3G, Remark 90.13.5 for (H3); 06J2 and 06J6 for (RS) = (H4)).

Give the tangent space its vector-space structure using (H2): addition comes from F(k[ε] ×_k k[ε]) ≅ F(k[ε]) × F(k[ε]) and the addition map k[ε] ×_k k[ε] → k[ε]; scalars act through the endomorphisms ε ↦ cε (Stacks 06IG, Definition 90.12.1; 06IH, Lemma 90.12.2).
Show (RS) implies (S1) and (S2) (Stacks 06J7, Lemma 90.16.6).

For a deformation functor and a surjection A′ → A whose kernel I is killed by m_{A′}, the set of lifts of ξ ∈ F(A), when nonempty, is a principal homogeneous space under T_F ⊗_k I (Stacks 06JI, Lemma 90.17.5).
acceptance: h_R = Hom_Λ(R, −) for R ∈ Ĉ_Λ satisfies (H1)–(H4).
The quotient of h_{k[[t]]} by t ↦ −t (characteristic of k not 2) violates (H2).

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms of functors, hulls and prorepresentability
nodes.statement: A natural transformation F → G of functors C_Λ → Set is smooth if for every surjection A′ → A in C_Λ the map F(A′) → F(A) ×_{G(A)} G(A′) is surjective. For R ∈ Ĉ_Λ and a formal element ξ ∈ lim_n F(R/m_R^n), the pair (R, ξ) is versal if the induced transformation h_R → F is smooth, and it is a hull (minimal versal) if in addition the induced map on tangent spaces T_{h_R} → T_F is bijective. F is prorepresentable if h_R → F is an isomorphism for some (R, ξ). A hull is unique up to non-unique isomorphism; in the classical coefficient setting, for F satisfying (H1) and (H2), a versal pair is a hull times a finite-variable power series ring. Without (H2), a ring-minimal versal object in the sense of Stacks 06T4 need not be a tangent-bijective hull.
hypotheses: Functors F with F(k) a point; Λ in the classical case for uniqueness statements.
proofSteps: Define smooth morphisms and compatible formal objects by Stacks 06HG and 06H3; define a hull as versal with bijective tangent map.

Keep Stacks 06T4 (minimality of the underlying ring) distinct from tangent-bijective minimality. Under H1 and H2 in the classical coefficient setting, Schlessinger gives a hull; smooth local maps between the resulting complete rings and Stacks 06T5 give the power-series factorization.
Uniqueness of hulls concerns an augmented Λ-algebra isomorphism compatible with the formal elements; the typed prototype records only the weaker ring-isomorphism consequence.
acceptance: h_R is prorepresentable with hull (R, id).
The identity transformation of any F is smooth.

nodes.title: Schlessinger's theorem
nodes.statement: Let Λ be a complete Noetherian local ring with residue field k (the classical case), and F : C_Λ → Set a functor with F(k) a point. (1) F has a hull iff F satisfies (H1), (H2) and (H3). (2) F is prorepresentable iff F satisfies (H1)–(H4), equivalently iff F is a deformation functor with finite-dimensional tangent space for which Der_Λ(k, k) → T_F is injective (the injectivity holds automatically in the classical case).
hypotheses: Classical case for the hull statement as stated; Stacks proves the general case with k/k′ separable.
For the classical hull and power-series criteria, Λ is a complete Noetherian local ring and Λ → k is its residue-field quotient (surjective with kernel m_Λ).
proofSteps: Existence of a versal object from (S1), (S2) and finiteness of T_F by successive approximation along small extensions (Stacks 06IW, Lemma 90.13.4), then a minimal versal object (Stacks 06T5).
The equivalence (1) is Stacks 06IX (Theorem 90.15.5) with Remark 06IY identifying it with Schlessinger's hull theorem.
Prorepresentability (2) is Stacks 06JM (Theorem 90.18.2), proved via (RS) ⇒ (S1),(S2) (06J7) and the existence of a hull, then injectivity of h_R → F using the torsor structure of lifts (06JI).
acceptance: The functor of deformations of a proper scheme with no infinitesimal automorphisms is prorepresentable (Stacks 0ET5).
The quotient functor of the deformation-functor non-example has no hull.

sources.match: Existence of versal and minimal versal formal objects under (S1), (S2), finite tangent space; the hull theorem identified with Schlessinger's; the prorepresentability criterion.

nodes.title: Obstruction theories for deformation functors
nodes.statement: For a predeformation functor F on C_Λ, an obstruction theory with values in a finite-dimensional k-vector space O assigns ob_e(ξ) ∈ O ⊗_k I for every small extension e : 0 → I → A′ → A → 0 and ξ ∈ F(A). The classes are natural for morphisms of extensions, including the induced linear maps on kernels, and vanish exactly when ξ lifts. The zero theory exists exactly when F is unobstructed. No choice of generator of I is part of this definition.
hypotheses: F is a predeformation functor; obstruction classes are natural with the induced maps on kernels. Hull statements additionally need the classical coefficient hypotheses and H1–H3.
proofSteps: Define the notion following the obstruction theories of Artin's axioms specialised to C_Λ (Stacks 07YG, Definition 98.22.1; examples 07YH, 07YI).
Smoothness of F is equivalent to the vanishing of every obstruction (Stacks 06HP, Definition 90.9.1 for unobstructedness).
A bound for the number of relations of a minimal hull presentation needs a separate verified argument; it is deferred to the recorded relation-bound gap.
acceptance: The zero obstruction theory exists exactly for unobstructed F, e.g. h_R with R a power series ring over Λ.

nodes.title: Square-zero deformations of algebras and the naive cotangent complex
nodes.statement: Let A′ → A be a surjection of rings with square-zero kernel I, A → B a ring map, N a B-module and c : I → N an A-linear map. A solution is an A′-algebra B′ with a surjection B′ → B whose kernel is a square-zero ideal identified with N compatibly with c. (1) Square-zero extensions of the A-algebra B by N are classified by Ext¹_B(NL_{B/A}, N). (2) If one solution exists, the isomorphism classes of solutions form a torsor under Ext¹_B(NL_{B/A}, N), and automorphisms of a solution form Hom_B(Ω_{B/A}, N). (3) If A → B is a local complete intersection (in particular smooth), a solution exists. (4) With the full cotangent complex L_{B/A} in place of NL the obstruction to existence lies in Ext²_B(L_{B/A}, N); with NL only the truncated statements (1)–(3) hold. For a scheme X flat over S and a first-order thickening S ⊂ S′, flat deformations of X over S′, when they exist, form a torsor under Ext¹_{O_X}(NL_{X/S}, f*C_{S/S′}) with automorphism group Ext⁰.
hypotheses: NL_{B/A} is the naive cotangent complex I/I² → Ω_{P/A} ⊗ B (Mathlib's Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex); B flat over A for the flat-deformation statements.
proofSteps: Rings: Stacks 0GPT (Lemma 91.2.3) for the classification, 08S7 (Lemma 91.2.2) for the torsor, 08S5 (Lemma 91.2.1) for maps between solutions, 08S6 (Lemma 91.2.9) for existence in the lci case.

The naive complex does not give an Ext² obstruction because its triangle is only close to distinguished (Stacks 0GPY, Remark 91.2.8); the Ext² obstruction with the full cotangent complex is Stacks 08SP (Lemma 92.16.1). This node uses only statements (1)–(3), which suffice for smooth and lci inputs, where NL ≃ Ω[0] or a two-term complex of projectives.
Schemes: Stacks 0D14 (Lemma 91.8.1) for flat deformations over a first-order thickening, using 063Y (Lemma 37.10.1) for flatness and 08UC, 08U8 for the ringed-space torsors.
Mathlib supplies Ω, H¹(NL) and the Jacobi–Zariski sequence; the Ext¹ classification of extensions is absent and is part of this node.
acceptance: For B = A[x] smooth, all solutions are trivial: Ext¹(Ω, N) = 0.
For B = A[x,y]/(xy − a) (lci) solutions exist and form a torsor under N/(x, y)N-type Ext¹.

sources.match: Classifies square-zero algebra extensions by Ext¹ of the naive cotangent complex, gives the torsor and automorphism statements and existence for lci maps, explains why no Ext² obstruction is claimed with NL, and gives the flat deformation torsor for schemes.

nodes.title: Deformations of smooth schemes and of line bundles
nodes.statement: Let Λ be a complete Noetherian local coefficient ring with residue field k, and X₀ a smooth separated finite-type k-scheme. The groupoid of flat deformations with a chosen special-fibre identification satisfies (RS). Its isomorphism-class functor satisfies H1 and H2; its tangent space is H¹(X₀,T), infinitesimal automorphisms are H⁰(X₀,T), and obstructions across a small extension of kernel I lie in H²(X₀,T) ⊗ I. Liftings with a chosen identification over the given A-deformation, up to isomorphisms preserving that identification, form an H¹(X₀,T) ⊗ I torsor when nonempty. For proper X₀, the isomorphism-class functor has a hull; H⁰(X₀,T)=0 suffices for prorepresentability. Given a flat thickening X_A ⊂ X_A′ and a line bundle L_A on X_A, liftings of L_A together with an identification on X_A form an H¹(X₀,O) ⊗ I torsor, with obstruction in H²(X₀,O) ⊗ I. The unframed fibre Pic(X_A′) → Pic(X_A) is a quotient by the boundary from H⁰(O_{X_A}^×), not automatically that torsor. On proper curves H² of quasi-coherent sheaves vanishes, so line bundles lift and smooth proper curves are unobstructed.
hypotheses: X₀ smooth over k for (1); proper for finiteness (2); (3) needs only X₀ proper and the exponential-free description of O^× on a square-zero thickening, 1 + I ≅ I.
proofSteps: Specialise SF.4/algebra-deformation-classes: for smooth X₀, NL_{X₀/k} ≃ Ω[0] with Ω finite locally free (Stacks 0D0N), so Ext^i(NL, O ⊗ I) = H^i(X₀, T) ⊗ I; local deformations are trivial by the lifting property of smooth affines (SF.4/smooth-lifting-torsor), and gluing local trivial deformations gives the H¹ torsor and the H² obstruction (Čech description).
Apply Stacks 0DY8 to the deformation groupoid, then 06JA to its isomorphism classes; use 0DY9, 0DYA and 0ET5 for the tangent, finiteness and hull statements. Do not infer H4 from groupoid RS.
For line bundles use 1 + I ≅ I and the exact sequence of Stacks 0C6R. Keeping the identification of the restriction gives the H¹ torsor; forgetting it also quotients by the boundary of H⁰ of units.
On a curve H² of a quasi-coherent sheaf vanishes (dimension one), so deformations and line bundles are unobstructed (Stacks 0DZQ for unobstructedness of one-dimensional lci schemes).
acceptance: Def_{P¹} is prorepresented by Λ (H¹(T_{P¹}) = 0, H⁰ ≠ 0 but the functor is trivial).
For an elliptic curve E₀ over k, Def has tangent space H¹(E₀, T) of dimension 1 and is unobstructed.

nodes.title: Versal deformation of a node
nodes.statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field and B₀ = k[[u, v]]/(uv). Over Λ (complete local with residue field k), the deformation functor of B₀ (flat deformations of the complete local k-algebra) has hull Λ[[t]] with universal deformation Λ[[t]][[u, v]]/(uv − t). More generally, for a nodal curve C₀ over k with nodes x₁,…,x_m, the map from global deformations of C₀ to the product of the local deformation functors at the nodes is smooth, and the deformations of a proper nodal curve are unobstructed; for a stable curve of genus g ≥ 2 the hull is Λ[[t₁,…,t_{3g−3}]] with the node x_i smoothed by the equation uv = t_i.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed; continuous deformations of the split complete local node, over a complete regular local coefficient ring Λ with residue field k as in DM69 §1 pp. 79–81; proper nodal C₀ for the global statement and stable for the dimension count.
proofSteps: Compute the naive cotangent complex for the finitely presented polynomial node k[u,v]/(uv), giving T¹ = k. Pass to continuous deformations of its completion only after the completion comparison in the recorded gap; ordinary algebraic Kähler differentials of k[[u,v]] cannot replace continuous differentials. The family uv=t gives the smoothing parameter (DM69 p. 81).

Global: the local-to-global spectral sequence for Ext(NL_{C₀}, O) has H²(C₀, T) = 0 on a curve, so global obstructions vanish and the map to local deformations is smooth (DM69 Proposition (1.5)); the dimension 3g − 3 is χ-computation via Riemann–Roch on the normalization (DM69 Theorem (1.6)).
de Jong 2.23 records the same local form over a general complete local base: B ≅ A′[[u, v]]/(Q − h).
acceptance: The node xy = 0 has a one-parameter versal deformation; the cusp y² = x³ has a two-parameter one (contrast).

nodes.title: The formal spectrum of an adic ring
nodes.statement: Let A be a ring that is complete and separated for the I-adic topology of a finitely generated ideal I (an adic ring with finitely generated ideal of definition; for example any Noetherian I-adically complete ring, or a p-adically complete ring with I = (p)). Spf A is the topologically locally ringed space whose underlying space is the closed subset V(I) of Spec A (homeomorphic to Spec A/I), and whose structure sheaf is O_{Spf A} = lim_n O_{Spec A/Iⁿ}, a sheaf of topological rings with Γ(Spf A, O) = A and Γ(D(f) ∩ V(I), O) = the I-adic completion of A_f. It does not depend on the choice of ideal of definition. For any adic ring B with ideal of definition J, morphisms Spf B → Spf A of topologically locally ringed spaces are in bijection with continuous ring maps A → B. Spf A is also the colimit, in the category of topologically locally ringed spaces (and as a functor on schemes), of the schemes Spec A/Iⁿ along the closed immersions Spec A/Iⁿ → Spec A/Iⁿ⁺¹.
hypotheses: A complete and separated for the I-adic topology, I finitely generated (Mathlib: IsAdicComplete I A together with I.FG).
The topology on sections is the inverse-limit topology.
proofSteps: Define the underlying space as the zero locus of I and the structure sheaf as the inverse limit of the structure sheaves of the thickenings Spec A/Iⁿ, all of which share this underlying space (the construction of EGA I §10 as reviewed in Stacks 0AHY, Section 87.2).
Independence of the ideal of definition: any two ideals of definition have powers contained in each other, so the inverse systems are cofinal.

Sections over basic opens are the completed localisations, using flatness and exactness of completion for Noetherian A (Mathlib's AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian and AdicCompletion.map_exact) and, in the finitely generated adic case, the standard Mittag-Leffler argument.
Morphisms Spf B → Spf A correspond to continuous maps A → B (Stacks 0AHY, equation 0AHZ); the colimit description is Stacks 0AIF (Definition 87.9.9).
acceptance: Spf Z_p has one point with O = Z_p; Spf k[[t]] has one point; Spf A with I = 0 is Spec A as a locally ringed space.

nodes.title: Formal schemes
nodes.statement: A formal scheme (of adic type with finitely generated ideals of definition) is a topologically locally ringed space 𝔛 that has an open cover by spaces isomorphic to Spf A for rings A complete and separated with respect to a finitely generated ideal. It is locally Noetherian if the A can be taken Noetherian. Morphisms are morphisms of topologically locally ringed spaces (continuous on sections, local on stalks). An ideal of definition is a quasi-coherent ideal 𝓘 ⊂ O_𝔛 restricting on affine pieces to ideals of definition; for each such 𝓘, X_n = (|𝔛|, O/𝓘ⁿ⁺¹) is a scheme and 𝔛 = colim_n X_n. A morphism f : 𝔛 → 𝔜 is adic if f*𝓙 · O_𝔛 is an ideal of definition for an ideal of definition 𝓙 of 𝔜; adic morphisms to Spf A correspond to compatible systems of schemes X_n over A/Iⁿ⁺¹ with X_n ≅ X_{n+1} ×_{A/Iⁿ⁺²} A/Iⁿ⁺¹. Schemes are the formal schemes with the zero ideal of definition.
hypotheses: Ideals of definition finitely generated (covers the Noetherian and the p-adically complete cases used by consumers).
Locally Noetherian is a separate predicate.
proofSteps: Define formal schemes as locally Spf in the category of topologically locally ringed spaces (the formal schemes of EGA I §10 as reviewed in Stacks 0AHY).
Construct the reductions X_n and the colimit presentation; affine-locally these are Spec A/Iⁿ⁺¹ (Stacks 0AIF).

Adic morphisms and the equivalence with compatible systems of schemes over the A/Iⁿ⁺¹: apply the colimit description of Stacks 0AIF levelwise and glue; the Noetherian characterisations are Stacks 0AID and 0AKM.
Fibre products of adic morphisms exist, computed affine-locally by completed tensor products (Spf of the completed tensor product).
acceptance: Every scheme is a formal scheme; Spf Z_p and the completion of P¹_{Z_p} along its special fibre are formal schemes.

sources.match: Formal schemes à la EGA as locally Spf objects of locally topologically ringed spaces, with the classical, adic, adic* and Noetherian classes and the locally Noetherian notion for formal algebraic spaces.

nodes.title: Formal completion along a closed subscheme
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme and Z ⊂ X a closed subscheme with quasi-coherent ideal 𝓘 of finite type (for example X locally Noetherian). The formal completion X/Z (also written X̂) is the formal scheme with underlying space |Z| and structure sheaf lim_n O_X/𝓘ⁿ restricted to Z; it comes with a canonical morphism X/Z → X. For X = Spec A and Z = V(I) with I finitely generated, X/Z ≅ Spf Â, Â the I-adic completion. Completion is functorial for morphisms f : X → Y with f(Z) ⊂ W. nodes.title: Coherent modules on Noetherian formal schemes and the completion functor
nodes.statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme, Z = V(𝓘) a closed subscheme and X_n = V(𝓘ⁿ). The category Coh(X, 𝓘) of coherent formal modules consists of inverse systems (F_n)_{n≥1} with F_n a coherent O_X-module annihilated by 𝓘ⁿ and isomorphisms F_{n+1}/𝓘ⁿF_{n+1} ≅ F_n; it is equivalent to the category of coherent O_{X/Z}-modules on the formal completion. When X = Spec A it is equivalent to finite modules over the I-adic completion Â. The completion functor Coh(O_X) → Coh(X, 𝓘), F ↦ F^ = (F/𝓘ⁿF)_n, is exact.
hypotheses: X Noetherian (or locally Noetherian); 𝓘 coherent.
proofSteps: Define Coh(X, 𝓘) as the category of compatible inverse systems (Stacks 0EHN, Section 30.23).

Affine case: (F_n) ↦ lim_n Γ(F_n) is an equivalence with finite Â-modules (Stacks 087W, Lemma 30.23.1), using Mathlib's AdicCompletion and its exactness on finite modules over Noetherian rings (AdicCompletion.map_exact).
The completion functor (Stacks equation 0880) is exact (Stacks 0881, Lemma 30.23.4), via flatness of completion.

The identification with coherent modules on the formal scheme X/Z is stated in Stacks 0EKN (Section 52.15); this node takes the inverse-system category as the working definition and records the comparison as API.

nodes.title: Theorem on formal functions
nodes.statement: Let A be a Noetherian ring, I ⊂ A an ideal, f : X → Spec A a proper morphism and F a coherent O_X-module. For every p ≥ 0 the canonical map H^p(X, F)^∧ → lim_n H^p(X, F/IⁿF) from the I-adic completion of the finite A-module H^p(X, F) is an isomorphism (and a homeomorphism for the limit topology). If A is I-adically complete, H^p(X, F) = lim_n H^p(X, F/IⁿF). Relative form: for f : X → Y proper with Y locally Noetherian, y ∈ Y, and X_n = X ×_Y Spec(O_{Y,y}/m_yⁿ), one has (R^p f_* F)_y^∧ ≅ lim_n H^p(X_n, F|_{X_n}).
hypotheses: A Noetherian; f proper; F coherent. Finiteness of H^p(X, F) over A is an input (coherence of higher direct images).
proofSteps: Coherence: R^p f_* F is coherent for proper f over a locally Noetherian base (Stacks 02O5, Proposition 30.19.1 [EGA III 3.2.1]); this is planned by Tau Ceti StableReduction Layer 2 (coherent pushforward under proper morphisms) and is used here as a prerequisite.

Apply the Artin–Rees type finiteness for the graded module ⊕ H^p(X, IⁿF) over the Rees algebra (Stacks 0897, Lemma 30.19.3, and 02OB, Lemma 30.20.4), with Mathlib's Ideal.exists_pow_inf_eq_pow_smul for the Artin–Rees lemma, to show the inverse systems are Mittag-Leffler and essentially the completion (Stacks 02OC, Theorem 30.20.5; Algebra 05GG).
The complete case is Stacks 087U (Lemma 30.20.6); the stalk form is Stacks 02OD (Lemma 30.20.7), via flat base change to the completed local ring.
acceptance: For X = P¹_A and F = O, both sides equal Â in degree 0 and vanish in degree 1.
Zariski's connectedness: for f proper with f_*O_X = O_Y, fibres are connected (consumer SF.4/stein-factorization).

nodes.title: Stein factorization and Zariski's connectedness
nodes.statement: Let S be a locally Noetherian scheme and f : X → S proper. Then f factors as X → S′ → S with S′ = Spec_S(f_*O_X), π : S′ → S finite, f′ : X → S′ proper with f′_*O_X = O_{S′} and geometrically connected fibres; S′ is the normalization of S in X. In particular, if f_*O_X = O_S then all fibres of f are geometrically connected. If S is normal and integral, X is reduced, every component of X dominates S, and H⁰(X_ξ, O) = κ(ξ) for the generic point ξ, then f_*O_X = O_S and f has geometrically connected fibres.
hypotheses: S locally Noetherian; f proper.
proofSteps: Finiteness of π from coherence of f_*O_X (Stacks 02O5, via Tau Ceti StableReduction Layer 2) and relative Spec of a finite quasi-coherent algebra (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0, relative Spec).

Connectedness of the fibres of f′ from the theorem on formal functions applied at points of S′: the completion of O_{S′} at a point is lim H⁰ of the thickened fibres, so idempotents of the fibre lift to the complete local ring, which is local (Stacks 03H0, Theorem 37.53.4).
The normal-base criterion is Stacks 0AY8 (Lemma 37.53.6); the identification of S′ with the normalization of S in X uses Mathlib's relative normalization (Scheme.Hom.normalization).
acceptance: A finite morphism is its own Stein factorization with f′ the identity; a proper curve over k with H⁰(O) = k has connected geometric fibres.

sources.match: Factorization of a proper morphism of locally Noetherian schemes into one with geometrically connected fibres and f′_*O = O followed by a finite map, S′ being the normalization of S in X; and the criterion over a normal base.

nodes.title: Grothendieck's existence theorem
nodes.statement: Let A be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal I, and f : X → Spec A a proper morphism. Then the completion functor Coh(O_X) → Coh(X, I O_X), F ↦ (F/IⁿF)_n, is an equivalence of categories onto coherent formal modules. More generally, for X separated of finite type over A, the completion functor is an equivalence between coherent O_X-modules whose support is proper over A and coherent formal modules whose support is proper over A/I. An algebraization includes a chosen compatible comparison F^ ≅ (F_n). Two algebraizations have a unique isomorphism inducing the specified formal comparison, by full faithfulness.
hypotheses: A Noetherian and I-adically complete (Mathlib IsAdicComplete with IsNoetherianRing).
proofSteps: Full faithfulness for proper X: Hom(F, G) is coherent, so Hom(F, G) = lim Hom(F_n, G_n) by the theorem on formal functions in the complete case (Stacks 0883, Lemma 30.24.1).

Essential surjectivity in the projective case: twist by an ample line bundle and use Serre vanishing and the theorem on formal functions to produce a presentation by sums of O(−d) (Stacks 0885, Lemma 30.24.3).

Proper case by Noetherian induction: Chow's lemma gives a projective X′ → X, an isomorphism over a dense open; push forward the algebraized systems from X′ and use the dévissage lemmas Stacks 088A, 088B (Lemmas 30.25.2–30.25.3) to conclude (Stacks 088C, Proposition 30.25.4).
General separated finite type case with proper support: Stacks 088E (Theorem 30.27.1), unwound in Remark 088F.
acceptance: For X = Spec A (finite over A), the theorem says finite A-modules = finite Â = A-modules; for X = P¹_{k[[t]]} every compatible system of line bundles O(d_n) is algebraized by O(d).

sources.match: Full faithfulness of completion for proper X, equivalence for projective X, the proper case via Chow's lemma and dévissage, and the general existence theorem for coherent sheaves with proper support.

nodes.title: Algebraization of closed formal subschemes and of morphisms
nodes.statement: Let A be Noetherian and I-adically complete, S = Spec A, S_n = Spec A/Iⁿ, X → S separated of finite type and X_n = X ×_S S_n. (1) A compatible system of closed subschemes Z_n ⊂ X_n with Z_n = Z_{n+1} ∩ X_n and Z_1 proper over S_1 is the system of reductions of a unique closed subscheme Z ⊂ X, and Z is proper over S; the same holds for compatible systems of finite morphisms Y_n → X_n. (2) If X is proper over S and Y → S is separated of finite type, then every compatible system of S_n-morphisms g_n : X_n → Y_n is the reduction of a unique S-morphism g : X → Y; equivalently Hom_S(X, Y) → Hom_{Spf}(X̂, Ŷ) is bijective.
hypotheses: A Noetherian, I-adically complete; separated finite type; properness of Z_1 (resp. X) over the closed fibre.
proofSteps: (1) Apply Grothendieck existence to the coherent formal module (O_{Z_n}) and the surjections O_{X_n} → O_{Z_n}; full faithfulness algebraizes the quotient map (Stacks 0899, Lemma 30.28.1); finite morphisms likewise (Stacks 09ZT, Lemma 30.28.2).

(2) Algebraize the graphs Γ_{g_n} ⊂ X_n ×_{S_n} Y_n by (1), then show the resulting closed subscheme is the graph of a morphism because its projection to X is an isomorphism after completion and hence an isomorphism (Stacks 0A42, Lemma 30.28.3).
acceptance: For X = Y proper, compatible automorphisms of the X_n come from a unique automorphism of X.

sources.match: Algebraization of compatible closed subschemes and finite morphisms with proper reduction, and of compatible morphisms from a proper scheme to a separated finite-type scheme.

nodes.title: Grothendieck's algebraization theorem
nodes.statement: Let A be Noetherian and I-adically complete, S_n = Spec A/Iⁿ. Let (X_n) be a compatible system of schemes X_n → S_n with X_n ≅ X_{n+1} ×_{S_{n+1}} S_n, X_1 → S_1 proper, and (L_n) compatible invertible sheaves on the X_n with L_1 ample on X_1. Then there is a proper scheme X over Spec A with an ample invertible sheaf L and isomorphisms X ×_S S_n ≅ X_n carrying L to L_n, compatibly in n. The pair (X, L) is unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with these identifications, and X is projective over A. Hence the formal scheme colim X_n is algebraizable, and its algebraization comes with the comparison X̂ ≅ colim X_n.
hypotheses: A Noetherian and I-adically complete; L_1 ample (the hypothesis cannot be dropped, see the acceptance test).
proofSteps: Form the graded A-algebra B = ⊕_d lim_n H⁰(X_n, L_n^{⊗d}); it is finitely generated in sufficiently divisible degrees by the projective case of Grothendieck existence and Serre vanishing (Stacks 0897).

Set X = Proj B (Proj of a graded algebra over the base ring; projective morphisms are part of Tau Ceti StableReduction Layer 2) and identify X ×_S S_n with X_n using the ampleness of L_n (ampleness lifts from X_1 to the thickenings X_n) and Stacks 0899 for the closed embeddings.
Uniqueness from SF.4/algebraization-of-subschemes-and-morphisms (2) (Stacks 089A, Theorem 30.28.4).
acceptance: Formal deformations of a smooth proper curve over k[[t]] are algebraizable (SF.4/effective-formal-deformations-of-curves).
Non-example of the hypothesis: Hironaka-type non-projective proper formal schemes (no ample L) need not be algebraizable.

sources.match: Given compatible proper X_n over A/Iⁿ with compatible invertible sheaves whose first term is ample, produces a proper X over A with ample L inducing them; proof via the section ring and the algebraization of closed subschemes.

nodes.title: Formal deformations of proper curves are effective
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete Noetherian local ring with residue field k and X₀ a proper scheme of dimension one over k (for instance a nodal or smooth projective curve). Let (X_n) be a compatible system of proper flat deformations X_n → Spec A/m^{n+1} of X₀. Then there is a proper flat scheme X → Spec A, projective over A, with compatible isomorphisms X ⊗ A/m^{n+1} ≅ X_n; X is unique up to unique isomorphism. In particular the versal formal deformation of a stable curve (SF.4/node-versal-deformation) is the completion of an algebraic family over the versal base, compatibly with its comparison to the completion.
hypotheses: X₀ proper of dimension ≤ 1 over k; deformations flat.
proofSteps: Choose an ample line bundle L₀ on X₀ (a proper curve over a field is projective).
Lift L₀ successively to L_n on X_n: the obstruction lies in H²(X₀, O_{X₀}) ⊗ (m^n/m^{n+1}), which vanishes on a curve (SF.4/deformations-of-smooth-schemes, part (3)).

Apply Grothendieck's algebraization theorem (SF.4/grothendieck-algebraization) to (X_n, L_n); flatness of X over A follows from flatness of the X_n by the local criterion of flatness for the completion.
acceptance: Effectivity for X₀ = P¹_k: the system is trivial and X = P¹_A.
The universal formal deformation k[[t]][[u,v]]/(uv − t) of a node is algebraized by the family xy = t inside a projective nodal curve.

nodes.title: Modifications and their centres
nodes.statement: Let S be an integral scheme. A modification of S is a proper morphism φ : S′ → S from an integral scheme S′ that is birational: there is a dense open U ⊆ S with φ⁻¹(U) dense in S′ and φ⁻¹(U) → U an isomorphism. When S is Noetherian the centre of φ is the closed subset of S over which φ is not an isomorphism (the complement of the largest such U). Modifications are closed under composition. A modification is in particular an alteration of generic degree one, but the two notions are kept as distinct predicates: an alteration is only generically finite.
hypotheses: S, S′ integral; φ proper.
Birationality is that of the morphism (an isomorphism over a dense open), which implies Mathlib's Scheme.Birational S′ S but is stronger: it is witnessed by φ itself.
proofSteps: Define the predicate on morphisms (Stacks 0AAZ, Definition 29.52.11; de Jong 1996, 2.17).
Composition: intersect the dense opens over which each map is an isomorphism; properness composes.
The centre is closed because the locus over which a proper birational morphism of Noetherian integral schemes is an isomorphism is open.

Finite modifications of a normal integral scheme are isomorphisms (Stacks 0AB1, Lemma 29.55.8); blowups of an integral scheme in a nowhere dense closed subscheme are modifications (Tau Ceti StableReduction Layer 4 blowup package).
acceptance: The blowup of 𝔸²_k at the origin is a modification with centre the origin.
Frobenius of 𝔸¹_{F_p} is not a modification.

sources.match: A modification of an integral scheme is a proper birational morphism from an integral scheme; finite birational morphisms to normal integral schemes are isomorphisms.

nodes.title: Strict transforms along blowups and modifications
nodes.statement: For a modification S′ → S of integral Noetherian schemes and a finite-type morphism X → S, de Jong’s base strict transform X′ is obtained from X ×_S S′ by killing sections locally annihilated by a nonzero element of the integral base S′. For a finite-type quasi-coherent module use the corresponding quotient by base torsion. If U ⊂ S is a dense open where X → S is flat and S′ → S is an isomorphism, X′ is the scheme-theoretic closure of X_U in X ×_S S′. Separately, the blowup strict transform imported from StableReduction Layer 4 kills exceptional-divisor torsion and is the closure over the full complement of the centre. It agrees with the base-torsion transform when X is flat over that full complement; flatness over some smaller dense open alone is insufficient. A closed subscheme flat over S′ and schematically equal to the full base change over a dense open is the base strict transform.
hypotheses: S and S′ integral Noetherian; X → S finite type; for the closure formula U is dense, X_U → U flat, and S′ → S an isomorphism over U.
proofSteps: Define the base-torsion quotient and prove transitivity as in de Jong 1996, 2.18 (p. 60; 2.20 extends the construction to alterations). A dense open of flatness and isomorphism identifies it with the schematic closure of the restricted family.

Import the blowup strict transform from StableReduction Layer 4. Stacks 080D–080E give its exceptional-torsion convention and identification with the blowup of X in the preimage of the centre. For comparison with base torsion require flatness on the full complement of the centre; the vertical-line test prevents conflating the two conventions.

Construct schematic closures by Mathlib’s Scheme.Hom.image of the restricted open immersion. For uniqueness use flatness over the integral modified base and schematic equality on a dense open; mere support containment is insufficient.
acceptance: For the blowup of 𝔸²_k at the origin, the Layer 4 blowup strict transform of the x-axis is the x-axis, whereas its base-torsion transform is empty because y kills its structure sheaf. Both transforms of the origin are empty.

nodes.title: Generic flatness
nodes.statement: Let f : X → S be a morphism of finite type with S integral, and F a quasi-coherent O_X-module of finite type. Then there is a dense open U ⊆ S such that X_U → U is flat and of finite presentation and F|_{X_U} is flat over U and of finite presentation. Algebraically: for a domain A, a finite-type A-algebra B and a finite B-module M, there is a nonzero a ∈ A with B_a and M_a free over A_a.
hypotheses: S integral; f of finite type; F of finite type.
proofSteps: Reduce to the affine case and prove generic freeness for finite modules over finite-type algebras over a domain (Stacks 051R–051S; Nitsure Lemma 4.1 gives the Noetherian case). Choose generators and a finite leading-term basis over the fraction field, then invert their finitely many nonzero coefficients to obtain a free module over the localized base. This generic-freeness theorem is part of the present target; no unchecked Mathlib spreading theorem is assumed.
Globalise by covering X by finitely many affines over an affine open of S (Stacks 052A, Proposition 29.28.1).
acceptance: For S = Spec Z and X = Spec Z[x]/(px), flatness holds exactly over U = Spec Z[1/p].

nodes.title: Flattening by blowing up (Raynaud–Gruson)
nodes.statement: Let S be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, U ⊆ S a quasi-compact open, X → S quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation, and F a quasi-coherent O_X-module of finite type with F|_{X_U} of finite presentation and flat over U. Here strict transform means the imported blowup/exceptional-torsion convention, which is defined without an integral-base hypothesis. Then there is a U-admissible blowup S′ → S (a blowup in a finitely presented closed subscheme disjoint from U) such that the strict transform of F is of finite presentation and flat over S′. In particular, if X → S is of finite type and quasi-separated with X_U → U flat and locally of finite presentation, then after some U-admissible blowup the strict transform of X is flat and of finite presentation over S′. For S Noetherian integral and X → S proper, this gives a modification S′ → S with centre outside U whose strict transform is flat (de Jong 2.19).
hypotheses: S qcqs; U quasi-compact open; finite presentation hypotheses as stated; no Noetherian hypothesis.
proofSteps: Reduce to an étale-local question on S and induct on the fibre dimension via the dévissage of Raynaud–Gruson (Stacks 0815, Theorem 38.30.7, with its étale-local form 0814 and the auxiliary results 080G, 080W, 05I3).
Compositions of U-admissible blowups are U-admissible blowups (Stacks 080L, Lemma 31.35.2), so successive flattening steps combine into one blowup.

Deduce the scheme version (Stacks 081R, Lemma 38.31.1) with F = O_X; for S Noetherian integral the U-admissible blowup is a modification with centre outside U, as used in de Jong 2.19 (where the projective case is argued via Hilbert schemes and the general case by citing Raynaud–Gruson 5.2.2). Once the resulting transform is flat over an integral base, it also equals de Jong’s base-torsion transform by the dense-open uniqueness statement; the two initial definitions are not identified unconditionally.
acceptance: For S = 𝔸²_k, U = S ∖ {0} and X the blowup of S at the origin viewed as an S-scheme, X is not flat over S but its strict transform under the blowup S′ = X → S is S′ itself, flat.

sources.match: Raynaud–Gruson flattening of a finite-type module flat over U by a U-admissible blowup, its scheme form, and the definition and composition of U-admissible blowups.

Constructs, for a projective (or locally projective, or proper with fibres of dimension ≤ 1) morphism over a Noetherian integral base, a modification with centre outside the flat locus whose strict transform is flat, citing Raynaud–Gruson Theorem 5.2.2 for arbitrary finite-type morphisms.

nodes.title: Modifications are dominated by admissible blowups
nodes.statement: Let S be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, U ⊆ S a quasi-compact open and φ : X → S a proper morphism with φ⁻¹(U) → U an isomorphism. Then there is a U-admissible blowup S′ → S that factors through X. In particular every modification of a Noetherian integral scheme is dominated by a blowup with centre in the complement of a dense open, and a separated finite-type X → S that is an isomorphism over U has strict transform open in some U-admissible blowup. Also: a separated, locally finite type, flat morphism that is an isomorphism over a retrocompact scheme-theoretically dense open U is an open immersion.
hypotheses: S qcqs; U quasi-compact; φ proper.
proofSteps: Apply flattening by blowup to φ: after a U-admissible blowup S′ → S, the strict transform X′ of X is flat and of finite presentation over S′ and an isomorphism over U.

A flat separated finite-type morphism that is an isomorphism over a scheme-theoretically dense retrocompact open is an open immersion (Stacks 081M, Lemma 38.11.5); being also proper and surjective it is an isomorphism, so S′ ≅ X′ → X gives the factorization (Stacks 081S, 081T, Lemmas 38.31.3–38.31.4).
p-adic instance used by Bhatt: for a proper morphism to Spec A that is an isomorphism after inverting p, the blowup can be taken in an ideal containing a power of p.
acceptance: A blowup in a nowhere dense centre is dominated by itself; the composite of two point blowups of 𝔸² is dominated by a single blowup in a finitely presented ideal supported at the origin (Stacks 080B).

sources.match: A proper morphism that is an isomorphism over a quasi-compact open is dominated by an admissible blowup; flat generic isomorphisms are open immersions; composites of blowups in finitely presented centres are blowups.

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.1 and Proposition 6.2, p. 11 (arXiv v2)

nodes.title: Chow's lemma
nodes.statement: Let S be a Noetherian scheme and f : X → S separated of finite type. Then there are n ≥ 0, a proper surjective morphism π : X′ → X and an immersion X′ → P^n_S over S, such that π⁻¹(U) → U is an isomorphism for some dense open U ⊆ X. Over a quasi-compact quasi-separated base the same holds without the dense-open clause. If X is integral, X′ can be taken integral and π is then a modification with X′ quasi-projective over S; if X is proper over S, X′ is projective over S.
hypotheses: S Noetherian (qcqs for the weak form); f separated of finite type.
proofSteps: Choose a finite affine cover of X in which each member contains every generic point (Stacks 0200 uses 28.30.4). Their intersection U is dense even when X is reducible. Replace X by the scheme-theoretic closure of U so U is schematically dense.
Embed each affine into projective space, take the closure of the diagonal image of U in the product, and use the Segre embedding.

The inverse images of the affine members glue: equality on the schematically dense U and separatedness identify their maps into X. Each inverse image is proper over its affine member, so the glued map is proper, surjective and an isomorphism over U (Stacks 0200).
acceptance: A proper non-projective variety (Hironaka's threefold) is dominated by a projective variety via a modification; a projective X needs no change (π = identity).

sources.match: Chow's lemma over a Noetherian base with the dense-open isomorphism clause, the H-projectivity remark, and the qcqs variant.

nodes.title: Alterations
nodes.statement: Let S be a Noetherian integral scheme. An alteration of S is a morphism φ : S′ → S from an integral scheme S′ that is proper, dominant, and finite over some nonempty open U ⊆ S. Equivalently (for S of finite dimension) φ is proper and dominant with dim S′ = dim S, or with the function-field extension K(S) ⊆ K(S′) finite. The generic degree of φ is [K(S′) : K(S)]; φ is generically étale iff this extension is separable. The centre of φ is the complement of the largest open of S over which φ is finite and flat. Alterations are closed under composition, and a modification is the same as an alteration of generic degree one, but an alteration need not be birational.
hypotheses: S Noetherian integral, S′ integral.
proofSteps: Define the predicate (Stacks 0AB0, Definition 29.52.12; de Jong 1996, 2.20).

Generic finiteness is equivalent to finiteness of the function-field extension: a proper morphism that is quasi-finite over the generic point is finite over a neighbourhood (Mathlib's IsFinite.iff_isProper_and_locallyQuasiFinite with the quasi-finite locus being open).

The function-field map K(S) → K(S′) is the stalk map at the generic point, which maps to the generic point by dominance; the generic degree is its finrank. Generically étale ⟺ separable uses Mathlib's Algebra.FormallyEtale.of_isSeparable at the generic point and spreading out.

Toolkit used by de Jong §5: finitely many alterations are dominated by one projective alteration (de Jong 5.4, via Chow's lemma); sections over an alteration of a dense open extend after a further alteration (5.5); a closed subset finite flat over S splits into sections after a finite normal alteration (5.6, using finiteness of normalization of excellent schemes); a proper surjection onto an integral scheme contains an alteration (Stacks 0DMN, closure of a multisection).
acceptance: Frobenius is an alteration of degree p, not generically étale and not a modification.
Spec Z[i] → Spec Z is a finite generically étale alteration of degree 2.

sources.match: An alteration of an integral scheme is a proper dominant morphism from an integral scheme that is finite over a nonempty open; a proper surjection onto an integral space contains an integral closed subspace mapping to it by an alteration.

Defines alterations, their centre, generic étaleness via separability of the function-field extension, strict transforms along alterations; proves domination of finitely many alterations, extension of sections after alteration, splitting of finite flat closed subsets into sections after a finite alteration, and the finite free local construction 5.7.

nodes.title: Strict normal crossings divisors
nodes.statement: Let S be a Noetherian scheme and D ⊂ S an effective Cartier divisor (a closed subscheme locally cut out by one nonzerodivisor), with irreducible components D_i, i ∈ I, taken with reduced structure. D is a strict normal crossings divisor if (a) O_{S,s} is regular for every s ∈ D; (b) D is reduced, i.e. D = ⋃ D_i scheme-theoretically; (c) for every nonempty J ⊆ I the scheme-theoretic intersection D_J = ⋂_{j∈J} D_j is regular of codimension #J in S (or empty). D is a normal crossings divisor if D ×_S S′ is a strict normal crossings divisor for some surjective étale S′ → S. Equivalently, at each point s ∈ D the local ring is regular and D is cut out by t₁⋯t_r for part t₁,…,t_r of a regular system of parameters, with the t_i defining distinct global components (strict case).
hypotheses: S Noetherian; effective Cartier divisors as closed subschemes.
proofSteps: Define as in de Jong 1996, 2.4, with effective Cartier divisors as closed subschemes from Tau Ceti StableReduction Layer 2 (effective Cartier divisors of sections) and Tau Ceti's Cartier divisor theory on integral schemes.
Local characterisation by part of a regular system of parameters (EGA IV 5.1.3 as cited by de Jong): regular quotients of regular local rings are cut out by parts of regular systems of parameters.
Pullback along smooth morphisms preserves the SNC property (used in de Jong 4.22, 6.16); the union of an SNC divisor with additional disjoint regular components meeting transversally stays SNC.

nodes.title: Making a normal crossings divisor strict by blowing up
nodes.statement: Let S be an excellent regular Noetherian scheme of pure dimension d and D ⊂ S a normal crossings divisor. Let D^(i) be the locally closed regular locus of points of D lying on exactly i local branches (i = 1,…,d). The composite φ : S̃ → S of the blowups S^(j+1) → S^(j) in the strict transforms of the closures of D^(d), D^(d−1), …, D^(2) is projective, an isomorphism outside the singular locus of D, S̃ is regular, and the reduced inverse image φ⁻¹(D)_red is a strict normal crossings divisor.
hypotheses: S excellent regular, D normal crossings.
proofSteps: Check étale locally on S, where D = V(t₁⋯t_r) with t_i part of a regular system of parameters; the strata D^(i) are regular and closures of the deepest strata are regular, so each blowup has regular centre and S^(j) remains regular (de Jong 1996, 7.2).
Blowing up the deepest stratum separates the branches through it; by induction the reduced total transform has components meeting in the expected codimension, i.e. is SNC.

nodes.title: Split semistable curves (de Jong)
nodes.statement: In de Jong's terminology a semistable curve over a scheme S is a flat proper finitely presented f : X → S whose geometric fibres are connected curves with at most ordinary double points; this is Tau Ceti StableReduction's prestable family (proper, at-worst-nodal of pure relative dimension one, geometrically connected fibres), which is the vocabulary used here (StableReduction's SemistableFamily is a different, stronger predicate). The singular locus Sing(f) is the closed subscheme defined by the first Fitting ideal of Ω_{X/S}; Sing(f) → S is finite, unramified and of finite presentation. A prestable family is split if for every s ∈ S the irreducible components of X_s are geometrically irreducible and smooth over κ(s) and every singular point of X_s is κ(s)-rational.
hypotheses: S any scheme; f prestable in the sense of Tau Ceti StableReduction Layer 3.
proofSteps: Take the prestable family predicate and Sing(f) from Tau Ceti StableReduction Layers 1 and 3 (Fitting ideal of Ω, finite unramified singular locus).
Splitness is a condition on fibres, preserved by base change (de Jong 1996, 2.22).
Local form at singular points of a split family: complete local ring A[[u, v]]/(uv − h) (SF.4/node-local-structure).

nodes.title: Local structure of a nodal family over a Noetherian base
nodes.statement: Let S be a Noetherian scheme, f : X → S a prestable family, x ∈ Sing(f) with image s, A = Ô_{S,s} and B = Ô_{X,x}. Then κ(x)/κ(s) is finite separable; there is a finite étale local extension A → A′ realising it, through which A → B factors, and B ≅ A′[[u, v]]/(Q(u, v) − h) with Q a quadratic form over A′ of unit discriminant and h ∈ m_{A′}. The trace of Sing(f) on Spec B is V(u, v) and maps to V(h). If f is split, B ≅ A[[u, v]]/(uv − h) with h ∈ m_A. Over a regular base S whose degeneracy locus is an SNC divisor V(t₁⋯t_r) at s, h = unit · t₁^{n₁}⋯t_r^{n_r}.
hypotheses: S Noetherian; f prestable; for the last clause S regular and f smooth outside an SNC divisor.
proofSteps: Sing(f) → S is finite unramified (Tau Ceti StableReduction Layer 1), so κ(x)/κ(s) is finite separable and a finite étale A′ exists; B is henselian (complete), so A → B factors through A′ (Mathlib's IsAdicComplete.henselianRing gives the Henselian property).

Modulo m_A the fibre has an ordinary double point, so B/m_A B ≅ κ(x)[[u, v]]/(q); lift q to Q and use flatness of B over A′ to get B ≅ A′[[u, v]]/(Q − h), then change coordinates using the unit discriminant to make h ∈ A′ (de Jong 1996, 2.23); the remark that the minimal versal deformation of a node is one-dimensional gives the same (SF.4/node-versal-deformation).
In the split case the two branches are rational, q splits as uv, and A′ = A.
Over a regular base with SNC degeneracy locus, V(h) ⊆ V(t₁⋯t_r) and regularity of A give h = ε t₁^{n₁}⋯t_r^{n_r} (de Jong 1996, 3.3).
acceptance: Over a DVR R with uniformiser π, this recovers Tau Ceti StableReduction Layer 1's local normal form R[u, v]/(uv − πⁿ) étale locally.

sources.match: Local description of semistable curves at singular points: complete local ring A′[[u,v]]/(Q − h), split case A[[u,v]]/(uv − h), with the singular locus V(u,v); over a regular base with SNC discriminant h is a unit times a monomial in the parameters.
The complete local ring of the universal stable curve at a node is a power series ring modulo xy − t_i.

nodes.title: Resolution of nodal families over a regular base (de Jong)
nodes.statement: Let S be an excellent regular scheme, D ⊂ S a strict normal crossings divisor, and f : X → S a split prestable family (split semistable curve) that is smooth over S ∖ D. Then there is a projective modification φ : X₁ → X with centre contained in Sing(X), such that X₁ → S is again a split prestable family smooth over S ∖ D and X₁ is a regular scheme. Before the final step one can arrange that Sing(X₁) has codimension at least three. The sections of f into the smooth locus lift to X₁.
hypotheses: S excellent regular; D SNC; f split prestable, smooth over S ∖ D.
proofSteps: Codimension-two components T of Sing(X) are regular, finite unramified over a component D_i, and carry an invariant n_T ≥ 2 from the local equation uv = ε t₁^{n₁}⋯; blowing up T keeps the family split prestable and lowers n_T by 2 (explicit three-chart computation); induct to get codim Sing ≥ 3 (de Jong 1996, Lemma 3.2 with 3.3–3.5).

With codim Sing(X) ≥ 3 the local rings are A[[u, v]]/(uv − t₁⋯t_μ); blow up components E of f⁻¹(D_i) that are not Cartier, using the two-chart computation; each blowup keeps the family split prestable and makes more components divisors, ending with X regular (de Jong 1996, Proposition 3.6).
Blowups and charts come from Tau Ceti StableReduction Layer 4; the local forms from SF.4/node-local-structure.
acceptance: Over a DVR, X = Spec R[u, v]/(uv − π³) is resolved by one blowup in the codimension-two singular locus followed by the point blowups, matching Tau Ceti StableReduction Layer 4's test case uv = πⁿ.

sources.match: Projective modification of a split semistable curve over a regular base, smooth off an SNC divisor, to a regular split semistable curve, by repeatedly blowing up codimension-two singular components (lowering the exponent by two) and then non-Cartier components of the preimage of D.

nodes.title: Generic linear projections
nodes.statement: Let k be a field and X ⊂ P^n_k a closed subscheme of pure dimension d < n containing a dense open subscheme geometrically reduced over k. There is a nonempty open U ⊆ P^n_k such that for every finite separable extension k′/k and p ∈ U(k′) with p ∉ X_{k′}, the projection pr_p : X_{k′} → P^{n−1}_{k′} from p is finite and (α) birational onto its image if d < n − 1, (β) finite étale over a nonempty open of P^{n−1}_{k′} (generically étale) if d = n − 1. Iterating, X admits a finite morphism to P^d_{k′} that is étale over a dense open and birational on a chosen generically geometrically reduced pure-codimension-one subscheme Z.
hypotheses: k a field; X projective of pure dimension d, generically geometrically reduced.
For simultaneous iteration on Z, assume Z generically geometrically reduced and pure of codimension one.
proofSteps: The statements are geometric; pass to a separable closure and reduce to X irreducible with a smooth k-point q (de Jong 1996, 2.11).
For d < n − 1 take p on a line through q meeting X only at q transversally; for d = n − 1 take p on a line meeting X transversally at q, so pr_p is unramified at q and Ω vanishes generically.
Such p sweep out a nonempty open set; finiteness because fibres are finite and X is projective.
acceptance: A smooth plane conic projected from a general point of P² is a degree-two generically étale map to P¹.

sources.match: Generic projections from points of projective space are finite, birational onto the image in codimension at least two and generically étale in codimension one, under a generic geometric reducedness hypothesis.

nodes.title: Fibring a variety in curves (de Jong 4.11–4.12)
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, X a normal projective variety over k of dimension d ≥ 1 and Z ⊂ X the support of a divisor. There is a finite set S of regular closed points of X disjoint from Z such that the blowup X′ → X in S admits a morphism f : X′ → Y′ onto a projective variety Y′ of dimension d − 1 (the Stein factorization of a morphism to P^{d−1}) with: (a) all fibres nonempty, geometrically connected and equidimensional of dimension one; (b) the smooth locus of f dense in every fibre; (c) generic fibre smooth; (d) the inverse image Z′ of Z finite over Y′ and étale over a dense open.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed; X normal projective variety; Z the support of a divisor.
proofSteps: Choose a finite morphism π : X → P^d étale over a dense open and birational on Z by iterated generic projection (SF.4/generic-projection); choose a general point p ∉ B ∪ π(Z) and project from p (de Jong 1996, Lemma 4.11).

X′ = {(x, ℓ) : π(x) ∈ ℓ} is the blowup of X in the finite set π⁻¹(p), contained in the regular locus and disjoint from Z; fibres of X′ → P^{d−1} are π⁻¹ of lines, of pure dimension one, and smooth near the exceptional fibres; Bertini for general linear sections gives a smooth fibre.

Take the Stein factorization X′ → Y′ → P^{d−1} (SF.4/stein-factorization) to make fibres geometrically connected; de Jong notes Y′ → P^{d−1} is étale and hence an isomorphism, but replacing P^{d−1} by Y′ avoids that input (de Jong 1996, 4.12).
acceptance: For a normal projective surface, the conclusion is a fibration X′ → Y′ over a curve whose fibres are connected curves, after blowing up finitely many points.

sources.match: After blowing up finitely many regular points away from Z, a normal projective variety maps to P^{d−1} with equidimensional one-dimensional fibres, dense smooth locus, a smooth fibre and Z generically étale over the base; the Stein factorization makes the fibres geometrically connected.

nodes.title: Adding sections meeting every fibre component three times
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed and f : X → Y a morphism of projective varieties whose fibres are nonempty, geometrically connected, equidimensional of dimension one, with smooth locus dense in every fibre. There is a divisor H ⊂ X, finite and generically étale over Y, such that for every geometric point ȳ of Y and every irreducible component C of X_ȳ, the set sm(X/Y) ∩ C ∩ H has at least three points.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed; f with the stated fibre properties.
proofSteps: Embed X by L^{⊗n} for a very ample L; the locus T of hyperplanes containing a fibre component has codimension at least n in P^∨ × Y, so for n ≫ 0 a general hyperplane section is finite over Y and transversal to a given fibre in its smooth locus (de Jong 1996, Lemma 4.13).
Each component of degree ≥ n ≥ 3 meets H in at least three smooth points over a neighbourhood; cover Y by finitely many such neighbourhoods (Noetherian induction) and take the union of the divisors.
acceptance: For a conic bundle over a curve, three general sections of O(1) give the required divisor.

sources.match: Constructs a relative divisor finite and generically étale over the base that meets every component of every geometric fibre in at least three distinct points of the smooth locus.

nodes.title: A stable model dominates the original family after modification
nodes.statement: Let f : X → S be a proper morphism of integral excellent schemes with sections σ₁,…,σ_n such that (a) all fibres are nonempty, geometrically connected and equidimensional of dimension one, (b) the smooth locus is dense in every fibre, (c) the generic fibre is smooth, (e) for every geometric point s̄ and every component C of X_s̄ at least three of the σ_i(s̄) are distinct points of C ∩ sm(X/S), and (g) there is a stable n-pointed curve (C, τ₁,…,τ_n) over S with an isomorphism β : C_U → X_U over a dense open U ⊆ S carrying τ_i to σ_i. Then after replacing S by a modification (and normalizing it), and C, X by their strict transforms, β extends to a birational S-morphism C → X.
hypotheses: S, X integral excellent; f proper with (a), (b), (c), (e), (g).
proofSteps: Let T ⊂ C ×_S X be the closure of the graph of β; after a modification of S, both X and T are flat over S (SF.4/flattening-by-blowup) and S is normal (de Jong 1996, 4.18).

Fibrewise: each component of X_s is dominated by exactly one component of T_s, and the projection T_s → C_s is non-constant on it; a constant projection would force three components of the stable fibre through one point or two marked points to meet, contradicting stability (de Jong 1996, Lemma 4.20).
Hence T → C is finite and birational; C is normal (Serre's criterion: flat over a normal base with reduced fibres and dense smooth locus), so T ≅ C and β extends (de Jong 1996, 4.21).
acceptance: If X is already the stable family, β is the identity and nothing changes.

sources.match: Under the fibre conditions and three-section condition, after a modification of the base making the family and the graph closure flat and the base normal, the graph closure is finite birational over the stable curve, hence equal to it, so the rational map from the stable curve extends to a morphism.

nodes.title: Altering a curve fibration to a split semistable curve (de Jong 5.8)
nodes.statement: Let f : X → S be a projective morphism of integral excellent schemes such that (a) all fibres are nonempty and equidimensional of dimension one and (b) the smooth locus of f is dense in every fibre. Then there are alterations ψ : S₁ → S and φ₁ : X₁ → X and a projective split prestable family (split semistable curve) f₁ : X₁ → S₁ with smooth generic fibre, with f ∘ φ₁ = ψ ∘ f₁. Given a proper closed subset Z ⊂ X, the diagram can be chosen with pairwise disjoint sections σ₁,…,σ_m of f₁ into sm(X₁/S₁) and a divisor D₁ ⊂ S₁ such that φ₁⁻¹(Z)_red ⊆ f₁⁻¹(D₁)_red ∪ σ₁(S₁) ∪ … ∪ σ_m(S₁).
hypotheses: S, X integral excellent; f projective with (a), (b).
proofSteps: Make the generic fibre smooth and geometrically irreducible by normalizing in a finite extension (de Jong 1996, 5.10); split Z's horizontal part into sections and blow up its vertical part (5.11, with Lemmas 5.5–5.6).
Add sections meeting every geometric fibre component in three smooth points after an alteration (Lemma 5.2), and sections through all singular points (Lemma 5.3).

Over a dense open the family with these sections is a stable pointed curve; using the projective cover of the moduli stack of stable pointed curves, alter S so that it extends to a stable pointed curve over S (5.13, via SF.4/stable-extension-after-alteration).

The stable model dominates X after modification (SF.4/stable-model-domination); replace X by it (5.14), then add sections again so that all singular points and fibre components are rational, which makes the family split (5.15–5.17).
acceptance: For a family of smooth curves over a curve S, the theorem yields the classical semistable reduction after a finite base change.

sources.match: Alters a projective curve fibration of integral excellent schemes with dense smooth locus into a projective split semistable curve with smooth generic fibre, with a given closed subset contained in sections and the preimage of a divisor, via the moduli of stable pointed curves and the domination lemma.

nodes.title: de Jong's alteration theorem
nodes.statement: Let X be a variety over a field k (an integral separated scheme of finite type over k, not necessarily geometrically integral) and Z ⊊ X a proper closed subset. There are an alteration φ₁ : X₁ → X and an open immersion j₁ : X₁ → X̄₁ such that (i) X̄₁ is a projective variety over k and a regular scheme, and (ii) j₁(φ₁⁻¹(Z)) ∪ (X̄₁ ∖ j₁(X₁)) is a strict normal crossings divisor in X̄₁. If k is perfect, φ₁ can be chosen generically étale. Moreover X̄₁ → Spec k factors through Spec k₁ for a finite extension k₁/k over which X̄₁ is geometrically irreducible and smooth; if k is perfect, X̄₁ is smooth over k.
hypotheses: X a variety over a field k; Z a proper closed subset.
proofSteps: Induction on d = dim X; d ≤ 1 by normalization (SF.4/resolution-of-curves) (de Jong 1996, 4.3).

Reductions (4.4–4.10): pass to the algebraic closure and descend to a finite extension (4.5); Chow's lemma makes X quasi-projective (4.6, SF.4/chow-lemma); compactify in projective space and add the boundary to Z (4.7); blow up Z to make it a divisor (4.8); normalize (4.10).

Fibre X in curves over a (d − 1)-dimensional variety (SF.4/curve-fibration), add a three-point divisor (SF.4/three-point-divisor), split Z into sections after a generically étale alteration of the base (4.16), extend the stable pointed curve over an alteration (SF.4/stable-extension-after-alteration, 4.17), and make it dominate X after modification (SF.4/stable-model-domination, 4.18–4.22).

Apply induction to the base with the discriminant divisor, giving a regular base with SNC degeneracy locus; resolve the semistable curve over it (SF.4/nodal-family-resolution, 4.23–4.27) and make the boundary strict (SF.4/nc-to-snc, 4.28).
Generic étaleness for perfect k: every alteration used is generically étale (4.4, 4.16, 4.17), and smoothness from regularity over a perfect field (2.10).
acceptance: For X a curve the theorem is normalization followed by a smooth compactification; for a singular surface X over C it gives a smooth projective surface X̄₁ with an open subset X₁ mapping to X by a generically finite proper map and SNC complement.
Over an imperfect field the alteration may be inseparable, and X̄₁ is smooth only over a finite extension k₁ of k (Remark 4.2).

sources.match: Every variety over a field has an alteration from an open subset of a regular projective variety with SNC complement containing the preimage of a given closed subset, generically étale over a perfect field; the remark gives smoothness over a finite extension.

nodes.title: Traits and varieties over a trait
nodes.statement: A trait is S = Spec R with R a complete discrete valuation ring; η and s denote its generic and closed points and π a uniformiser. A morphism of traits Spec R′ → Spec R is given by a local homomorphism R → R′ of complete discrete valuation rings sending π to a nonzero element; its ramification index is e = v_{R′}(π). It is a finite extension of traits when R′ is finite over R. An S-variety is an integral separated scheme X, flat and of finite type over S; equivalently (X being integral) X is integral, separated and of finite type over S with nonempty generic fibre X_η. The special fibre X_s = V(π) is a principal divisor on X. For a finite extension of traits S′ → S and an S-variety X, every irreducible component of X ×_S S′ (reduced) is an S′-variety and maps to X by an alteration.
hypotheses: R complete DVR; X integral separated flat of finite type over S.
proofSteps: Define traits via Mathlib's IsDiscreteValuationRing together with completeness for the maximal ideal (IsAdicComplete) (de Jong 1996, 2.12, 2.15).

Compare finite extensions of traits with Tau Ceti's FiniteDVRExtension: for complete R the integral closure in a finite separable extension is a complete DVR, so the package's chosen prime is unique and its localRing is R′.
Generic and special fibres are Tau Ceti's genericFiber and specialFiber; flatness of an integral X over R is equivalent to π not being a zero divisor, i.e. X_η nonempty.
Base change along a finite extension of traits: X ×_S S′ → X is finite and flat, so each component dominating X gives an alteration (de Jong 1996, 6.8).
acceptance: Spec Z_p is a trait; Spec Z_(p) is not.

sources.match: Defines complete DVR morphisms with ramification index, traits and finite extensions of traits, S-varieties as integral separated flat finite-type schemes, and base change along finite extensions of traits.

nodes.title: Strictly semistable varieties over a trait
nodes.statement: Let S be a trait and X an S-variety; let X_i (i ∈ I) be the irreducible components of X_s and X_J = ⋂_{j∈J} X_j scheme-theoretically. X is strictly semistable over S if (a) X_η is smooth over κ(η); (b) X_s is reduced, X_s = ⋃ X_i scheme-theoretically; (c) each X_i is an effective Cartier divisor on X; (d) for every nonempty J ⊆ I, X_J is smooth over κ(s) of codimension #J in X. Then X is regular, and at x ∈ X_s lying on exactly X_1,…,X_r the complete local ring is B[[t₁,…,t_r]]/(t₁⋯t_r − π) with B formally smooth over R, X_i = V(t_i); a neighbourhood of x is smooth over Spec R[t₁,…,t_r]/(t₁⋯t_r − π). If X is proper, (b)–(d) imply (a); if κ(s) is perfect, (b)–(d) say exactly that X_s is an SNC divisor on X.
hypotheses: S a trait; X an S-variety.
proofSteps: Define via conditions (a)–(d) (de Jong 1996, 2.16).

Local description: B = Â/(t₁,…,t_r) is formally smooth over κ(s) by (d), lift B to a formally smooth R-algebra and a section of Â/πÂ → B, then lift the surjection B[[t]] → Â and identify the kernel (de Jong 1996, 2.16, using 2.8).
Regularity follows from the local form; for perfect residue field smoothness of X_J is regularity (2.10), giving the SNC reformulation.
acceptance: Spec Z_p[x, y]/(xy − p) is strictly semistable.

sources.match: Defines strictly semistable S-varieties by smooth generic fibre, reduced special fibre whose components are divisors with smooth intersections of the right codimension, derives the local form B[[t₁..t_r]]/(t₁⋯t_r − π) and regularity, and the reformulations for proper X and perfect residue field.
